evals.prompt: Preflight a proposed TypeScript notification module before coding. Production needs one EmailNotifier. The proposal also exports Notifier, NOTIFIER_TOKEN, NotifierRegistry, createNotifierFactory, mergeNotifierOptions, and six optional lifecycle callbacks so tests can inject FakeNotifier. No second production notifier or configuration override is planned.
evals.expected_output: Requests revision of fake-only seams and unused configurable surface, describes the direct production-complete design, and records rejected extension points without turning the result into a post-implementation review.
assertions: A test fake is explicitly rejected as production variability evidence.
The registry, token/interface layer, or configurable factory is rejected as unsupported.
A concrete dumb version and abstraction ledger are included.

evals.prompt: Preflight a payment service design with one production StripePaymentGateway behind a PaymentGateway port. The port isolates Stripe SDK types from the domain, owns idempotency and error translation, and is a committed package contract. Tests also use a fake. Decide whether to keep the port before implementation.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the single-implementation port because it contains an external protocol and committed contract; distinguishes the fake from the real justification and proposes no hypothetical gateways.
assertions: The justification cites protocol containment or committed public contract, not the test fake.
No hypothetical extra gateway is proposed.
The abstraction ledger records the boundary exception.

evals.prompt: Preflight a job runner used by three production commands. All three repeat the same cancellation, timeout, metrics, and cleanup lifecycle, but their job bodies and success outputs differ. The team proposes a runJob({ execute, onSuccess }) helper plus a plugin registry, strategy hierarchy, per-hook middleware, and twelve optional callbacks.
evals.expected_output: Keeps a small lifecycle helper supported by three consumers, rejects the speculative plugin machinery, and describes a direct vertical implementation.
assertions: The shared lifecycle helper is retained with evidence from three production consumers.
The plugin registry, strategy hierarchy, middleware, or optional hook surface is rejected.
A concrete dumb version is described.
